headline: Labour cuts £2bn from Army front line
deck: Armoured vehicle variants scrapped as defence chiefs warn of gaps in capability
body: Mortar, repair and overwatch versions of the Boxer armoured vehicle have been dropped, leaving the army to find other ways to fill gaps in its front-line capability. Ministers confirmed in answers to parliament that almost two billion pounds had been removed from the programme, which was meant to form the backbone of the mechanised infantry. Senior officers said the decision would leave units without specialist vehicles for several years, while the Ministry of Defence said the requirement would be met in other ways. The opposition said the cuts showed the government was not serious about defence, weeks after promising to raise spending as a share of national income.
